title: Richest 1% emit more carbon than the world’s poorest, says Oxfam
content: The world’s richest 0.1 per cent, a group of just 8 million people, emit more carbon than the poorest 44 per cent of the global population, or 3.5 billion people, combined, according to a report by Oxfam, an international non-profit focused on tackling poverty and inequality.

title: Greenhouse gases hit record highs in 2025, locking in further global warming, warns WMO
content: Another year, another record. Concentrations of carbon dioxide (CO₂) and other human-induced greenhouse gases in the atmosphere reached unprecedented highs in 2025, committing the planet to further long-term warming, according to the latest WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin . Atmospheric concentrations of these gases continue to rise, driving changes in the global climate. The past 11 years have been the warmest on record, says the report by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), which assesses greenhouse-gas levels through 2025.

title: Let’s not bury our heads in sand
content: Climate change and social inequities are intensifying global crises, with wealthy nations failing to meet their responsibilities. The youth's protests reflect frustration over rising temperatures, economic instability, and inequality. Immediate action is needed to address these issues and create a fairer, more sustainable world for future generations. The world is on fire. But who will put out the flames when we are so caught up in multiple crises and trapped in a habit of procrastination? These polycrises are related, each feeding on the other—much like a flesh-eating bacteria. We need to get our heads out of the sand and start behaving like adults, rather than pushing away the changes that we need to be serious about. Let’s do a reality check.
